resources.title: NIST Software Portal (code.nist.gov)
resources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.cite_note: The #/ALLSOFTWARE fragment never reaches the server. Catalogue contents are UNCONFIRMED. Cite the portal root.
resources.verdict_qualifier: surfaces one GAP against this repository
resources.one_line: The federal release pattern is directly copyable. This repository ships no LICENSE.

licensing_model.basis: 17 U.S.C. 105 - not subject to copyright in the United States
licensing_model.foreign: copyright may subsist outside the United States
licensing_model.notice: NIST-developed software is provided by NIST as a public service. You may use, copy, and distribute copies of the software in any medium, provided that you keep intact this entire notice.
conditions: provided AS IS, no warranty of merchantability, fitness, or non-infringement
no liability for use or results
modified versions must carry notice of the change, its date, and its nature
third-party components carry their own statements

gaps.gap: No LICENSE, COPYING, NOTICE, CITATION.cff, or code.json anywhere in the repository tree. Verified by directory walk 2026-08-08. The repository is published via GitHub Pages and targeted at cloud.gov.
affects: schema/usmc-issuance-2.0.xsd and NAMESPACES.md - the artifacts most likely to be adopted externally
data/exports/*.xml - leave the repository with no statement of authority on them
gaps.fix: Add LICENSE stating applicable terms, and NOTICE carrying the not-authoritative disclaimer in the NIST AS-IS form. Consider a processing instruction or header comment carrying the disclaimer into exported XML.

actions.action: Emit code.json at the repository root, per the Federal Source Code Policy. tools/emit_dcat.py is the natural home.
actions.note: Not a requirement. No agency inventory currently pulls this repository.

transfers: Catalogue-over-repositories pattern, validated by federal precedent - mirrors docs/sources.html and config/revision_index.json.
Disclaimer attached to the artifact rather than to the website.

resources.publisher: Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey - apparent, not confirmed
resources.retrieval_error: robots.txt could not be fetched or parsed; request refused. Reproduced on both https://fast.mfr.nps.edu/ and https://fast.mfr.nps.edu
resources.public_search: No result names this host or expands the acronym. Four query formulations run.
resources.one_line: Host refuses automated retrieval. No public documentation names the tool.
discharge_requires: Landing-page, About, and documentation text pasted from a browser session
The acronym expansion and the owning NPS organisation
Whether it is publicly reachable or CAC-gated
second_pass_questions: Documents or structure? Documents compete with or feed canonical/. Structure is a different axis, likely NOT APPLICABLE as Monterey Phoenix was.
Stable identifiers? Check for collision against the NAMESPACES.md grammar in the /us/dod/don/usmc/ space.
API or bulk export? Would relax the human-in-the-loop acquisition constraint in REFERENCES.md.
Authority status? An NPS research product cannot promote a record to VERIFIED.

resources.publisher: Skillsoft Books24x7, via University of Maryland Global Campus EZproxy
resources.retrieval_error: Authenticated proxy redirect. Resolves only for a signed-in UMGC account. No bibliographic metadata recoverable from the URL.
resources.one_line: Authenticated proxy link. Title and author not recoverable from the URL.
resources.citation_rule: Cite the book, not the proxy. The EZproxy link is institution-scoped, session-scoped, and vendor-keyed, so it cannot resolve for a reader outside UMGC and is not durable.
second_pass_questions: Does it contradict a ruling already in NAMESPACES.md or conformance-matrix.md? A contradiction is a finding; agreement is not.
Primary or secondary? A textbook is secondary by construction and can never be the text a verdict turns on.
Current or historical? Pre-2015 technical titles follow the section 11 precedent: doctrinal ancestor, live descendants bind.

resources.title: EU Open Source Solutions Catalogue
resources.verdict_qualifier: as a source; REJECTED as a dependency
resources.one_line: 1,076 solutions and none for legal-rule encoding. Metadata schema transfers, code does not.
resources.core_finding: No catalogued solution targets legislation markup, legal-rule encoding, or decision automation. Closest tags are compliance-management (30) and workflow-management (76), both process tooling.
transfers: Aggregate-do-not-host pattern, a second federal-scale precedent alongside the NIST portal.
Per-entry metadata schema, serviceable as-is for a GOATS solutions register.
Development status as a published first-class field. This project publishes no equivalent for its own tools.
rulings: No code from this catalogue enters this repository until a LICENSE exists and the specific candidate's terms are cleared against it.
EUPL and other copyleft terms are incompatible with a 17 U.S.C. 105 public-domain target in the direction that matters: a derivative of copyleft code cannot be placed in the public domain.
unconfirmed: Per-entry licences. EUPL dominance is a characterisation of European public-sector practice, not a count taken from this catalogue.
Exhaustive walk of all 54 pages was not performed. The absence finding is drawn from the taxonomy and the visible result set.

resources.title: LEOS - Legislation Editing Open Software
resources.repo_note: MinBZK is a Ministry of the Interior fork describing itself as a proof of concept not meant for production. That is the fork's status, not upstream LEOS's. Upstream is at code.europa.eu and was not retrieved.
resources.format: XML, Akoma Ntoso V3 (OASIS LegalDocML), AKN4EU instantiation
resources.platform: containerized web application; Docker Compose and Kubernetes manifests present
resources.verdict_qualifier: not a drop-in replacement for SemperScribe; not a component of this repository
resources.one_line: Stable EU drafting platform emitting Akoma Ntoso. Models EU legal acts, not naval correspondence. EUPL and containers fail two reuse gates.

reuse_gates.licence: FAIL - EUPL-1.2 copyleft against a 17 U.S.C. 105 target, and no LICENSE exists here yet. Applies to forking into this repository, not to running LEOS as a separate system.
reuse_gates.standalone: FAIL - containerized web application; build.sh must succeed on a fresh clone
reuse_gates.scale: FAIL - drafting platform against a static-site encoding project
reuse_gates.substitution: PARTIAL - would replace SemperScribe, not repository code
reuse_gates.exit: PASS - stable, actively released, EU institutional maintainer

resources.argument_for: Akoma Ntoso output satisfies INTEGRATION-SEMPERSCRIBE.md requirement R2 by construction, removing the largest unknown in that design and replacing a proprietary NLDP with an OASIS standard interface.
resources.argument_against: Models EU legislative instruments in AKN4EU. A Marine Corps Order under MCO 5215.1K - Situation, Mission, Execution, Cancellation - is not one of those. Teaching it means maintaining a fork of an EUPL web application.
decision_tree: 1. Ask whether SemperScribe meets R2, structured provisions with native designators. One conversation.
2. If yes, build the Option A bridge and this question closes.
3. If no, evaluate LEOS as a SEPARATE system emitting AKN, never as a fork inside this repository.
4. Either way, require structured XML export with native designators, and prefer AKN over a private format.
unconfirmed: Full technical prerequisites - language, framework, repository backend. The fork exposes only Dockerfiles and shell; upstream at code.europa.eu was not retrieved.
The AKN4EU versus MCO 5215.1K structural mismatch is a reasoned conclusion from both models, not a quoted statement.
